basis: Craniosynostosis, limb anomalies and intellectual disability define the syndrome; structural eyelid anomalies occur in 30-79%; renal anomalies are occasional.
Heterotaxy with cardiac defects (~33%); chronic sinusitis 2/2, chronic otitis media 2/3, and duodenal atresia/malrotation 1/3 each; situs reversal alone causes no damage.
Neoplasm originates in the biliary tract, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease affecting the rectum and distal colon.
FRRS1L-related encephalopathy causes severe developmental impairment, epilepsy and movement abnormalities; hypotonia and spasticity are neurologic manifestations.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; an underlying structural brain disorder is not specified.
Mesenchymal soft tissue sarcoma, usually arising in deep extremity connective tissues; histologic subtype does not imply additional organ involvement.
Cerebral impairment of color recognition despite preserved color perception; no intrinsic eye damage is established.
Diffuse gastric carcinoma originates in and infiltrates the stomach.
Inherited keratinization disorder of palmar and plantar skin.
Inherited corneal endothelial dystrophy causing corneal abnormalities and opacity.
Corneal epithelial disease with adherent mucus-epithelial filaments; infection or an immune-mediated mechanism is not intrinsic to this diagnosis.
Isolated inherited scalp-hair structural disorder; retinal abnormalities and cataracts occur in only 5-29%.
Epiphyseal dysplasia, microcephaly and intellectual disability define it; pigmentary retinopathy with field loss occurs in ~33%; restrictive physiology lacks direct lung pathology.
Roseolovirus infection umbrella; the common roseola rash is transient, and encephalitis belongs to a minority subtype.
PAX8-related thyroid dysgenesis or hypoplasia causes congenital thyroid hormone deficiency; no common additional organ damage is established.
Metabolic bone disorder with loss of bone strength and fragility fractures associated with postmenopausal estrogen deficiency.
FZD4-related retinal vascular development disorder causing vitreoretinal pathology; localized retinal vessels do not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Hereditary Wilms tumor originates from nephrogenic blastemal cells in the kidney; associated syndromic abnormalities are not universal.
Progressive skeletal hyperostosis with muscle atrophy and contractures; hearing, optic nerve, neurologic and cardiac complications are each reported in 5-29%.
Inherited iron metabolism disorder with inappropriate hepcidin regulation and hypochromic microcytic anemia; other tissue manifestations are uncommon.
Marrow failure; renal malformations, microphthalmia and hearing loss each 2/3; impaired GH response (2/3) and skeletal defects (~1/3) omitted at cap.
Primary skeletal muscle disease with progressive distal weakness, fatty replacement and myofiber pathology; no peripheral nerve disease is established.
NAPB-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound intellectual disability; visual impairment is unlocalized and does not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Cerebral arteriopathy with infarcts and destructive white-matter disease; retinopathy in 2/2 supports ocular involvement; scoliosis alone does not establish direct skeletal disease.
